chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Lucille, Louise and Rosita on Fifth Avenue
summary: She tells of Stumpy Buddy and of two young women, Lucille and Louise, who followed musicians; their wildness at clubs, and Sammy Price expecting the piano to vanish.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Stumpy Buddy was a terrific trombonist...

They put them in the music scene because they followed all the musicians. They were crazy about musicians but they were two beautiful girls and I think their father was a big political leader and a wonderful Italian man off of Fifth Avenue. Fifth Avenue was a pretty rough street; after jam sessions certain nights we'd all go there. Lucille and Louise were not allowed out, not unless their mother asked me if I was going along with them. I don't know why she thought I could protect them. They were both older than what I was by 2 years. There was another friend of mine - Louise, Lucille, and Rosita (Shewing,) I'm telling you they was something else. I didn't have one chance to sit in on a jam session after we went out together because the whole town practically was destroyed. These two little girls (I think they were between 18 and 20 years old), they'd go in a night club and if they took a couple of drinks or so, they'd just take the pictures off the wall. Sammy Price happened to be playing in the club one night and he was a

terrific boogie-woogie pianist and they always liked to go to see him. The minute he saw us coming up the stairs he said, 'Well, I guess I better go home,' because he was expecting the piano to disappear. They had such a ball. We'd go down to Fifth Avenue where their Dad was. It was pretty rough down there.
